tools.title: Fleet overview

This is the right first call for any general "how is everything" question. The numbers are the same ones the Glow dashboard shows.

tools.name: find_plugin

tools.name: pending_updates
tools.title: Pending updates
tools.description: Plugin, theme and core updates outstanding across the fleet, one client, or one website, ordered by the most outstanding first. These are the counts Glow last recorded from each site, not a live check. A site that is not connected still reports the counts from when Glow last reached it: those are historical, not outstanding work, which is why fleet_overview excludes them from its totals.

client.description: Client name. Omit for the whole fleet.

tools.name: add_website_guide
tools.title: How to add a website
tools.description: The steps to connect a new WordPress site to Glow, with the agency's own dashboard link and how many sites it currently manages. Use this when asked how to add, connect or onboard a site, or how to get started. Pass the site's domain if the user has given it, to get a direct link to the plugin install page on that site; ask for it if not. tools.name: run_safe_update
tools.title: Update plugins safely
tools.description: Update named plugins on ONE website using Safe Updates, which takes a backup and screenshots first, verifies the site afterwards, and can be rolled back. Requires the website uuid, which you must get from a read tool first: this tool does not accept domains. List the plugins explicitly by name; there is no "update everything" option. Updates are dispatched in the background, so use safe_update_status to see how they went.

website_uuid.description: The website uuid from site_updates, find_sites or list_websites. Must be a uuid, not a domain: this tool will not guess which site you meant. Also accepted as "website".

website.description: Alias for website_uuid. Still requires a uuid.

plugins.description: Plugin names to update, exactly as reported by site_updates or find_plugin. Every plugin is named explicitly. pending_updates gives counts, not names: call site_updates for the names and the uuid this tool needs.

data.description: Rows for a query, or the resulting record for a write. Empty when nothing matched.

truncated.description: True when more records matched than were returned.

limit.description: The limit applied, when one was.

hint.description: Why the result is empty or truncated, and what to do about it.

tools.name: run_update
tools.title: Update themes or WordPress core
tools.description: Update named themes, or WordPress core, on ONE website. These updates CANNOT be rolled back: unlike plugin updates there is no backup, no before-and-after check and no undo, which matches how Glow itself performs them. For plugins use run_safe_update instead, which is reversible. Requires the website uuid from site_updates. Name themes explicitly; there is no "update everything" option.

website.description: Website uuid from site_updates. A uuid, not a domain.

themes.description: Theme names exactly as site_updates reports them.

core.description: Update WordPress core to the latest version available on the site.

tools.name: add_custom_work
tools.title: Log custom work on a website
tools.description: Record a piece of work against ONE website, so it appears on the timeline and in the client report. Requires the website uuid. Time is given in minutes. By default the time counts against that site's monthly allowance; pass counts_toward_allowance false to log it as free of charge. Use time_allowance to see what is left before logging.

website.description: Website uuid. A uuid, not a domain.

description.description: What was done. Shown to the client, so write it for them.

minutes.description: How long it took, in minutes. Omit for work with no time against it.

who.description: Who did the work. Defaults to the account the connection belongs to.

completed_at.description: When the work was done, ISO 8601. Defaults to now.

counts_toward_allowance.description: Whether the time comes out of the monthly allowance. Default true.

show_in_client_report.description: Whether it appears in the client report. Default true.
